title: 2024 Energy Consumption Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report presents the findings from the 2024 energy consumption analysis, focusing on total and per-building-type usage, quarterly trends, half-year changes, tariff and meter usage, commercial load on hot days, and the distribution of consumption and temperature. The analysis reveals significant insights into energy consumption patterns and their implications for business stakeholders.

key_findings.statement: The total energy consumption for 2024 was 1,207,699.96 kWh, with an average of 845.73 kWh per reading across 1,428 readings.

Energy consumption varied significantly by building type, with Industrial (995,362.16 kWh) consuming the most, followed by Commercial (196,367.15 kWh), and Residential (15,970.65 kWh) consuming the least.
Energy consumption showed a quarterly trend with the highest consumption in Q4 (352,881.81 kWh) and the lowest in Q3 (264,863.12 kWh).
There was a 4.71% increase in energy consumption from the first half (589,955.03 kWh) to the second half (617,744.93 kWh) of the year.
Commercial buildings consumed an average of 415.29 kWh on hot days (temperature >= 25°C), with 19 such readings recorded.

The median energy consumption was 406.8 kWh, with a standard deviation of 913.44 kWh. The mean temperature was 11.61°C, with 62 readings missing temperature data. The Pearson correlation between temperature and energy consumption for commercial buildings was -0.638.

Energy consumption during peak hours was 599,624.07 kWh, representing 49.65% of total consumption, while off-peak consumption was 608,075.89 kWh. There were 12 unique meters, with the highest usage meter consuming 252,241.26 kWh.

limitations: The analysis is based on a limited dataset from 2024, which may not fully represent long-term trends.
Missing temperature data for 62 readings could affect the accuracy of temperature-related findings.
The correlation between temperature and energy consumption for commercial buildings is moderate, indicating other factors may influence consumption.
conclusion: The 2024 energy consumption analysis provides valuable insights into consumption patterns, highlighting the significant role of industrial buildings, seasonal variations, and the impact of temperature on commercial consumption. These findings can inform strategic decisions and energy management practices for business stakeholders.
